prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1457; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver. Vehicles were traveling in opposite directions at low speed when the front ends made contact. Both drivers reported they were able to exit their vehicles under their own power. Scene photos requested from the insured.

Entry 2: Claimant reports a knee injury sustained in the impact and states she sought initial evaluation at an urgent care facility. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has asked for a direct explanation of the claims process. Explained the bodily injury coverage available under the policy and the documentation needed, including treatment records and itemized bills.

Entry 3: Obtained the claimant's written statement. She describes braking before contact and reports pain and swelling in the right knee that limited her ability to bear weight the following morning. Medical authorization form sent to claimant for signature. Vehicle damage appraisal scheduled at the repair facility of her choice.

Entry 4: Appraisal completed. Damage is confined to the front bumper assembly, hood, and headlamp housing on the claimant's vehicle, consistent with the reported low-speed impact. Reviewed photographs from both vehicles and found the damage patterns compatible with the loss description. Liability analysis in progress.

Entry 5: Received treatment records from the claimant's provider documenting a knee sprain with a recommendation for physical therapy and follow-up imaging. Claimant confirmed she is continuing care and will forward bills as they arrive. Reserve reviewed and file remains open pending completion of treatment and final medical documentation.
